per_dimension.notes: Definitions of “militant-involved” and specific group matching (e.g., TTP) vary widely: some use inter1/2 categories, others rely on text '%militant%' or numeric interaction codes, and the code sets differ across queries. TTP matching predicates differ across queries and columns searched.
All relevant queries consistently filter country = 'Pakistan'. Place-specific filters (e.g., KP province, cities) are not reused elsewhere, so no cross-query inconsistency arises.

Year windows for 2024 and for 2023–2024 are expressed equivalently (year IN vs date bounds). The 'last 12 months' window is inconsistent across queries (rolling day vs full calendar months vs a fixed 'as of' date).

Event/target categorization varies: 'militant attacks/clashes' alternates between event_type lists vs actor-based selection; police/security-targeted definitions differ (notes/tags vs interaction text vs none). Interaction/target role classification also differs (symmetrical interaction vs inter2-only).
Per-actor 'events_count' is deduplicated by event in one query but not another. Monthly unique militant actor counts are consistently computed with COUNT(DISTINCT).

All queries consistently filter to Pakistan; no cross-query omission of country or scope expansion detected. Use of different table names (events vs acled_events) appears cosmetic here without evidence of different populations.

conflicts.explanation: Q14 treats interaction roles symmetrically; Q22 depends on actor2 coding only. Events where role order differs will be categorized inconsistently.

conflicts.predicate_a: Count(*) over union-all actor1/actor2 rows (no DISTINCT by event_id per actor)
conflicts.predicate_b: SELECT DISTINCT event_id_cnty per actor before counting; counts de-duplicated per actor
conflicts.explanation: Q16 may double-count if an actor appears as both actor1 and actor2 in the same event (or due to duplicates), while Q20 deduplicates by event per actor. Resulting 'events_count' is not comparable.

summary: There are substantial inconsistencies in how “militant-involved” events and specific groups (notably TTP) are defined across queries. Temporal windows for the “last 12 months” and target-category definitions (e.g., police/security-targeted) also diverge, leading to result-changing differences. Yearly windows and geography are consistent, and some aggregation methods are aligned, but overall consistency is moderate at best.
